name: Hypoplastic Right Heart Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Hypoplastic Right Heart Syndrome

criteria.description: Underdevelopment or severe hypoplasia of the right ventricle
Pulmonary valve atresia or severe stenosis leading to obstruction of right ventricular outflow
Presence of an atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale facilitating right-to-left shunting
Clinical evidence of central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunting
Echocardiographic confirmation of right heart structural abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of right ventricular hypoplasia, pulmonary valve atresia or stenosis, and atrial septal defect confirmed by echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings combined with clinical presentation of cyanosis and heart failure in neonates.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia
Severe underdevelopment of the right ventricle detected clinically and by imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulmonary valve atresia or severe stenosis

common.notes: Rapid breathing due to heart failure and hypoxia
Common in neonates due to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: tiredness and poor feeding in infant

common.notes: Systolic murmur due to turbulent flow across stenotic valves or septal defects
Enlarged liver secondary to right heart failure

occasional.notes: Irregular heart rhythms secondary to structural abnormalities
Transient loss of consciousness due to poor cerebral perfusion

rare.notes: Due to paradoxical embolism through septal defects
Secondary to increased pulmonary vascular resistance
Infective complication in structural heart disease

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating hypoplastic right ventricle, pulmonary valve atresia/stenosis, and atrial septal defect
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and decreased pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be sporadic or associated with chromosomal anomalies
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement and right axis deviation

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary valve atresia with intact ventricular septum
No atrial septal defect required for survival

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
references: Moss and Adams' Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents, 9th Edition
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease
